title: The Sign That Saved the Shop
illustrationIdea: A small flower shop beside a train station, with a large black handwritten board outside and two people stopping to read it.

paragraphs.en: Mr. Lin [[owned]] a small flower shop in Tainan. It stood next to a [[busy]] train station. Ten years ago, people came every day. But last spring, the shop was almost empty. Mr. Lin looked at his [[sales]] [[report]] and felt sad.
paragraphs.zh: 林先生在台南開了一間小花店。花店就在忙碌的火車站旁邊。十年前，每天都有客人上門。但去年春天，店裡幾乎沒有人。林先生看著他的銷售報表，心情很低落。

paragraphs.en: His daughter Amy had an idea. She was a college student. The old [[sign]] outside was small and dirty. Amy said, "People walk by too fast." She bought a big black board. Then she wrote a short line on it [[by hand]].
paragraphs.zh: 他的女兒艾咪想到一個辦法。她是個大學生。外面那塊舊招牌又小又髒。艾咪說：「大家走得太快了。」她買了一塊大黑板。然後她用手寫上一句短短的話。

paragraphs.en: The line was simple. It said, "Buy one flower for a stranger today." Some people stopped and smiled. A young man bought a rose for the bus driver. A woman [[ordered]] ten flowers for her [[office]]. The shop was busy again by noon.
paragraphs.zh: 那句話很簡單。上面寫著：「今天為一個陌生人買一朵花。」有些人停下腳步，露出微笑。一個年輕男子買了一朵玫瑰送給公車司機。一位女士為她的辦公室訂了十朵花。中午之前，店裡又忙了起來。

paragraphs.en: Mr. Lin changed the [[message]] every week. Each line was short and warm. [[Customers]] took photos of the board. They [[shared]] the photos online. Soon new people came from other cities. Some of them waited outside before nine.
paragraphs.zh: 林先生每週都換上新的訊息。每一句都簡短又溫暖。客人們拍下黑板的照片。他們把照片分享到網路上。很快就有人從其他城市過來。有些人不到九點就在門外等候。

paragraphs.en: Now the shop [[delivers]] flowers to hotels and banks. Mr. Lin still writes the sign by hand. He never uses a printer. "A machine can print," he says. "But a machine cannot say hello."
paragraphs.zh: 現在這家店會把花送到飯店和銀行。林先生還是親手寫招牌。他從來不用印表機。「機器會印字，」他說。「但機器不會打招呼。」

questions.q: What is the main idea of the article?
options: The train station brought many people to the shop.
Amy wanted to open her own flower shop.
A simple sign written by hand helped a small shop.
Flowers are cheaper in Tainan than in other cities.
questions.explanation: 全文從第二段艾咪寫下手寫招牌開始，到第三、四段生意變好，都在說一塊手寫招牌救了小店，故選第三項。

questions.q: What did Amy write on the board?
options: Buy one flower for a stranger today.
We are open every day until nine.
All flowers are half price this week.
We deliver to hotels and banks.
questions.explanation: 第三段第二句直接引用招牌上的句子「Buy one flower for a stranger today.」，故選第一項。

questions.q: How did people in other cities hear about the shop?
options: Mr. Lin called them on the phone.
The bus driver told them.
Amy sent them letters.
Customers shared photos of the board online.
questions.explanation: 第四段說顧客拍照並把照片分享到網路上，接著才有其他城市的人來，故選第四項。

questions.q: Why does Mr. Lin still write the sign by hand?
options: Because a printer costs too much money.
Because he thinks writing by hand feels warm.
Because Amy is too busy to help him.
Because he cannot read very well.
questions.explanation: 第五段最後他說機器會印字卻不會打招呼，可推論他認為手寫比較有人情味，故選第二項。

title: The Wrong Meeting Room
illustrationIdea: A nervous young man in a shirt standing at an open meeting room door while ten seated coworkers turn to look at him.

paragraphs.en: Kevin started his first [[job]] at Sunrise Foods last May. On his second day, his [[boss]] sent him to Room 502. Kevin was nervous and walked very fast. On the fifth floor, he got out and turned left. Then he opened the door of Room 520.
paragraphs.zh: 凱文去年五月在陽光食品開始了他的第一份工作。上班第二天，他的主管要他去 502 會議室。凱文很緊張，走得很快。他在五樓走出電梯後往左轉。然後他推開了 520 會議室的門。

paragraphs.en: Ten people sat around a long table. They all turned and looked at him. A woman smiled and pointed at an empty chair. Kevin sat down and said nothing. The [[meeting]] was about a new fruit drink.
paragraphs.zh: 十個人圍著一張長桌坐著。他們全都轉過頭來看他。一位女士微笑著指了指空位。凱文坐下來，什麼也沒說。這場會議在談一款新的果汁飲料。

paragraphs.en: The team had a problem. Their new [[product]] did not sell well. A [[manager]] asked, "Does anyone have an idea?" Kevin looked at the small bottle on the table. He said, "The [[package]] is hard to open. My grandmother could not open it."
paragraphs.zh: 這個團隊遇到了問題。他們的新產品賣得不好。一位經理問：「有人有想法嗎？」凱文看著桌上的小瓶子。他說：「這個包裝很難打開。我奶奶就打不開。」

paragraphs.en: The room became very quiet. Then everyone started to talk at the same time. The manager wrote Kevin's [[suggestion]] on the board. After the meeting, she asked for his name. Kevin told her about his [[mistake]]. She laughed and said, "Please come again next week."
paragraphs.zh: 會議室頓時安靜下來。接著所有人同時開口說話。經理把凱文的建議寫在白板上。散會後，她問了他的名字。凱文把自己走錯會議室的事告訴她。她笑著說：「下週請再來一次。」

paragraphs.en: Two weeks later, Kevin's team joined the [[project]]. They [[tested]] a new bottle with older [[customers]]. The [[cost]] went up only a little. But orders grew by thirty percent.
paragraphs.zh: 兩週後，凱文的團隊也加入了這個專案。他們找年長顧客測試新瓶子。成本只增加了一點點。但訂單卻成長了三成。

paragraphs.en: Kevin still tells this story to new workers. He always says the same thing. "Ask a simple question," he tells them. "A wrong room can still be the right one."
paragraphs.zh: 凱文到現在還會把這個故事說給新進同事聽。他每次都說同樣的話。「問一個簡單的問題，」他這樣告訴他們。「走錯的房間，也可能是對的房間。」

questions.q: What is the main idea of the story?
options: Kevin was late for a meeting on his first day.
Kevin's mistake led to a good idea and new work.
Sunrise Foods needed to hire more young workers.
Fruit drinks sell better in summer than in winter.
questions.explanation: 第一段凱文走錯會議室，第三、四段他的建議被採用，第五段兩個團隊合作，全文主軸就是一個錯誤帶出好結果，故選第二項。

questions.q: Why did Kevin walk into Room 520?
options: His boss gave him the wrong room number.
He wanted to meet the manager there.
The elevator stopped on the wrong floor.
He was nervous and turned the wrong way.
questions.explanation: 第一段說主管叫他去 502，但他很緊張、走得很快、出電梯往左轉，才走錯門，故選第四項。

questions.q: What problem did the team in Room 520 have?
options: Their new drink did not sell well.
Their meeting room was too small.
Their manager was going to leave.
Their team had too many new workers.
questions.explanation: 第三段第二句明說新產品賣得不好，故選第一項。

questions.q: Why did the manager ask for Kevin's name?
options: She wanted to tell his boss about him.
She needed help to move the chairs.
She thought his idea was useful.
She knew his family very well.
questions.explanation: 第四段她把凱文的建議寫在白板上，散會後才問名字，還請他下週再來，可推論她覺得這個建議有用，故選第三項。
